## Findings refused (left as drafted)

- U17 · i ("did not come to the end of them"): the note already gives the rival reading (not delivering them) and both rest on Ming 不到 alone. Left; the note carries the doubt.
- U4 · aburun, -urun glossed "converb of time: when -ing" while the note says "simply 'taking'": the glossary's bolurun entry has the same label, and the note explains the sense. Left.
- U31 · Qān-(n)i-jan Seṅgüm-i as apposition; U34 · erelesü "let me take"; U43 · accusative Kököčü aγtači-ji read as subject: all flagged uncertain in the notes and the l keeps the case; no better reading from the Ming. Left.
- ge- 'to cast aside' (U31, U40, U44): matches the published entries for gežü, gebe. A completive auxiliary is likely (čabčižu gebe = "cut down"), but the glossary entry is the house line. Left; see doubts.
- -dqun "imperative, polite plural": glossary uses "plural command"/"polite plural imperative" interchangeably. Left.
- U25 · "crept up on them" for marijažuγ̇u: i loose but l and note exact. Left.
- U21 · "fell in with" for orožuγ̇u: note says "came into the hands of". Left.
- U1 · Suldudai kept as a clan name in l and i (Ming 姓(名)); glossary has Süldüsün 'the Suldus' but the printed form differs. Left.
- Morph "Kököčü, a boy's or man's name": follows the glossary.

## Remaining doubts

- γ rendering in names is not uniform in the house: Qahan (γ→h), but Taqai, Sorqaqtani, Dongqaid (γ→q). Taqai and Dongqaid are fixed by the glossary; Sorqaqtani is new and follows them. Owner may want a rule.
- ge-: is it the 'say/do' auxiliary rather than 'cast aside'? Would change gežü, gebe, and the i of U44 ("cut him down and cast him aside").
- U30 speaker, U34 optative/conditional -sü, U17 kürgen, U18 who cuts whom, U21 usurγarun subject: all genuinely open from the Ming alone.
- Sub-glossary check (gloss.json) is for pass 2.

## House renderings for conventions.md (added by 186-188)

- Names in `i`: Taqai-Ba'atur (with Suldudai kept as printed), Jaqa Gambu (not hyphenated), Ibaqa-Beki, Sorqaqtani-Beki, Tolui, Badai, Kishiliq, Wang Qan, Qori-Sübechi, Kököchü, Senggum, Eme (a wife, not a name), Didig-Saqal, Negün-Usun, Chul, Abji'a-Ködegeri, Olon-Dongqaid, Tümen-Tübegen, Ongjid Kereid, Jirgin, Naiman.
- γ̇ → ' (Abji'a), as Ba'atur, Cha'ur, Ongjid.
- tusa-jin in-ü / an-u tula → "in return for the service of …"; amin žaγ̇ura → "at risk of one's life" (uncertain); kilgün (Ming 轅條) "shaft"; nögöġe kilgün bol → "Be a second shaft!".
- Decree formula: žarliγ bolurun → "issued a decree:"; -dqun → "plural command"; oluγsaγ̇ar / alaγsaγ̇ar → "take it as you win / kill it".
- aγtači (Ming 管馬的) → "groom" in `i`, "gelding-keeper" in `l`; emutü → "wife-having"; noγai miγ̇urtai → "dog-faced".
- Ming 名的 for ündür: 'name' reading noted; ündür "high" kept.


# Review, pass 2 (units.json and gloss.json) — secret-history-186-188

Files read: conventions.md, run3/RUNBOOK.md §2, packet.md, units.json, gloss.json, novel-forms.json, known-forms.json, review.md (pass 1) and the published glossary. No translation opened or recalled. `units.json` and `gloss.json` edited in place by script; `t` strings and the number of words and of morphs per word verified identical before and after (45 units, 354 words); every gloss.json entry's final Ming bracket re-checked against novel-forms.json (93/93 identical) and every entry against the format `<dictionary form> — <meaning> (<grammar>) [<Ming gloss>]` (93/93). Units are numbered U0–U44 as in pass 1.

Counts (per changed field; 41 changes): critical 0 · major 0 · moderate 11 · minor 25 · nit 5.

## Method for gloss.json
Each of the 93 new entries was read against (a) the word in the packet and its Ming gloss, (b) the unit's morph for it, (c) the published glossary (stems and wording already there), (d) the key convention (the reader's tokens: Tolui-(j)a gives `tolui` + `ja`; šiltaγ̇an(i)-jar gives `šiltaγ̇ani` + `jar`). The 4 `__broaden__` entries each equal the existing glossary entry whole + ' · ' + the new reading (checked by string prefix against secret-history-glossary.json); the ' · also …' form is the convention and none deviated. No modern forms were found invented; the faults were scope (entries describing a neighbouring token), plurals, and clashes with the published glossary.

- beki: U4 note, Ibaqa-Beki and Sorqaqtani-Beki morphs and both gloss entries now say "a title of rank, uncertain", as the glossary does for Cha'ur-Beki, Qachi'un-Beki, Toqto'a-Beki (it is borne by men too); "lady" is gone.
- qaγ̇uluγ̇asu: lemma qaγ̇ulu- → qaγ̇ul- (unit and gloss); the suffix stays -uγ̇asu, as in oluγ̇asu beside it.
- qatara-: the glossary has "urge on, gallop" (Ming 點); the part's morphs/entries said "ride or walk to and fro" and "was riding". Entries now give both and call the reading uncertain; l and i of U28/U38 unchanged.
- tolui, šiltaγ̇ani: entries rewritten to describe only their own token (the suffixes are the known entries ja and jar); jar is broadened for 'because of'.
- Broadened beyond the glosser's 4: ündür-ün (Ming 名的), jar ('because of', Ming 因), tebčižü (Ming 捨着, nit). The glosser's own 4 (ögüġesü, mün, göreġesün, kököčü) kept; kököčü's "the groom Kököchü" made general; ögüġesü marked uncertain.

## Findings refused (left as drafted)

- saγ̇uγsaγ̇ar "of a tent, to stand pitched": reads as pinned, but it is flagged "sense from the Ming 全具; uncertain" in both the unit and the entry; no better reading from the Ming alone. Left.
- Ming-spelling variants against the published entries (tebčižü aside): 屈下 / 服下了, 外面 / 在外, 入了來 / 投入有來, 說呵 / 說了, 妻 行 / 婦人 行, 做者 / 可, 子孫的 / 子子, 直到 / 到了 etc. The sense is the same; broadening every one would bury the entries. Left, except where the unit's reading depends on the Ming (ündür-ün, jar).
- Tümen-Tübeġen (printed ġ) against the published Tümen-Tübegen (key tümen-tübegen-i): the keys differ because the print differs, so a separate entry is right; the dictionary form follows the print. Left; owner may want the two spellings unified.
- Entries naming stems "inferred from the Ming" (qubija-, doraita-, žisü-, qoruγ̇a-, usurγa-, udqu-, uγ̇u-, oru-, qaṅγa-, tügeġe-, tügele- …): all hedged as uncertain, none contradicts the published glossary; I cannot test them further without a dictionary. Left.
- qulad "qulan — wild ass" against Ming 野馬 "wild horses": the glossary has no qulan for the animal; qulan is the standard word and the entry quotes the Ming. Left.
- kürüġe "wine-set", asaraγsad "those who have tended", čul "perhaps 'desert'": all flagged uncertain in entry and note. Left.
- U1 "Taqai-Ba'atur himself received the hundred Jirgin" (about says "rewards Taqai-Ba'atur"): note calls it an inference; about states it flatly. Left; tiny.

## Remaining doubts

- qatara-: whether the house sense 'urge on, gallop' should replace 'to and fro' in U28 (l/i) as well; left to the owner (U38 'rode off' already fits it).
- ge- (U31, U40, U44) 'cast aside' vs the 'say/do' auxiliary: unchanged from pass 1.
- Doubled 'because' structure, the speaker in U30, and the roles in the nested quotation U34–U37: open from the Ming alone, flagged in the notes.
- The glossary ending -tele/-te (tügelete) and the reading of tügele- are guesses from Ming 勾.
- Tümen-Tübeġen / Tümen-Tübegen spelling, and the γ→q rule in names (Sorqaqtani), are for the owner.
